brief: Zero Hedge frames the session as 'making room' for the Anthropic IPO: a dynamic it says is even more visible than before SpaceX's debut, with software weak and Anthropic's tokenized price tracking NVDA lower as investors raise cash. Hawkish FedSpeak (Waller urging a 50bp December move if a January hike isn't signaled, Barr backing further hikes, Daly more measured) and hawkish FOMC Minutes pushed December hike odds marginally higher, still only 10-15% for 50bp, yet Treasuries rose a third straight day on a solid 20Y auction and the dollar hit fresh 18-month highs, because a 4% WTI drop on inventory builds triple consensus eased inflation pass-through fears despite active Iran and Ukraine strikes. Gold fell to its lowest since September 2025 and bitcoin sold off as crypto and precious metals funded IPO liquidity; NVDA gave back its Kress-call gains and Dow lagged on UNH. Goldman's desk saw quiet flows with hedge funds buying and long-onlys selling. Bloomberg's Simon White argues gold is cheap but not a liquidity hedge, so weakness doesn't void its solvency-hedge case.
